newsitem.title: GERMANY: Ford-Werke chief seeks to cut costs-report.
newsitem.headline: Ford-Werke chief seeks to cut costs-report.

text.p: The leader of Ford Motor Co's German operations said in a magazine interview on Wednesday that he wanted to impose new cost-saving measures to help return the unit to profitability.

William Boddie, who was named to the position as chairman of Ford-Werke AG's management board last June, said in the interview with Germany's "Manager Magazine" that a few production areas were unproductive and must be restructured.
"We are not happy with our cost structure," he told the magazine in its latest issue.
He also said the Cologne-based unit would remain in the luxury market with its Scorpio vehicle, saying production and quality issues with the car have been solved.
"I want to see clear progress in quality," he said. "We must also sell more high-value vehicles and dramatically reduce our costs."
In addition, he wanted to rein in personnel costs, saying overtime should not be taken into account for holiday, Christmas and sick pay benefits.
Boddie said about 30,000 Scorpios were sold in 1995 but only about 11,000 in 1996, with the goal for 1997 rising to about 25,000 vehicles.
"I can guarantee you that we are clearly going to sell more Scorpios."
